If this were my question, either reply would serve equally well. Both correctly explain that a TCP connection consists of two independent byte streams requiring four logical operations (announcing and acknowledging both initial sequence numbers) compressed into three packets via piggybacking. Both also accurately articulate why a two-way exchange fails: the server cannot confirm that the client received its ISN, and stale duplicate SYNs would create phantom half-open connections without the client having an opportunity to reset them. Because both answers align completely with the protocol facts without material error, there is no meaningful difference.
